To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the JC virus can infect the kidneys of AIDS subjects.

JC virus infection in the kidney was found in 6.3% of AIDS subjects; the viral infection was lytic in all the cases; major rearrangements of transcriptional control regions were found in all three cases; and no point mutations were detected in the viral protein region.
JC virus can be found in the kidneys of AIDS subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible role of JC virus as a cofactor in renal damage in AIDS patients.
the role of JC virus as a cause of nephropathy in AIDS patients.
the identification of the JC virus in renal tissue of AIDS subjects, and the analysis of the genomic sequences of the transcriptional control and viral protein 2 region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the JC virus can be considered a potential etiological factor for renal disease in AIDS subjects.
the JC virus is rarely present and does not seem to be a major cause of renal damage, although it may be involved in the pathogenesis of some cases.
JC virus is a possible cause of kidney damage in AIDS subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
JC virus can replicate within the kidney of AIDS subjects and that this replication can be associated with morphological evidence of virus-induced damage.
JC virus can be found in the kidney of AIDS subjects and that it may play a pathogenic role.
, although the JC virus is not a major pathogen in renal disease, it can be a cofactor for the development of nephropathy in some AIDS subjects, especially those with low CD4+ counts.
